Orphaned process (ppid=1) executing from /tmp hidden hex path (post-dropper stage-2) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts processes reparented to init/systemd (ppid=1) whose image or command-line resolves to /tmp/.<6-12 hex chars> — the exact reparenting + execute-from-deleted-path shape left behind by the Laravel-Lang stage-2 loader after it backgrounds via `php "$f" > /dev/null 2>&1 &` and rm-deletes its own dropper files. Visible in process telemetry even after the file is unlinked. Rationale: Anchors on the article's explicit process IOCs: 'an orphaned php process with ppid=1' and 'an orphaned unnamed ELF process with ppid=1, executing from a now deleted path under /tmp'. Combines the reparent-to-init shape with the /tmp/.<hex> path generated by bin2hex(random_bytes(6)). Survives the self-delete because process metadata is captured at exec time.
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1564.001 T1070.004 T1620
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Containerised PHP daemons in misconfigured images where init=systemd and app binaries live under /tmp
  • CI runner cleanup jobs that detach via nohup and reparent to init
  • Snap-confined apps whose mount squash lands binaries under /tmp/...
  • Custom build agents using mktemp -d in /tmp/.<hex> as a working dir for daemonized helpers
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath startswith "/tmp/snap." or FolderPath startswith "/tmp/.mount_" or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("snapd","systemd-tmpfiles"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: snapshot /proc/<pid>/exe (resolves to the deleted path on Linux even after unlink), /proc/<pid>/environ, /proc/<pid>/maps, and /proc/<pid>/fd before killing — these survive the rm-self-delete and are the highest-fidelity forensic source. Capture all outbound network connections from the PID. 2) Contain: kill the orphan PID and any siblings sharing the same hidden hex base; isolate the host; preserve memory if the host is critical (the binary runs from memory after the on-disk artefact is gone). 3) Hunt: pivot to UC1 (egress to flipboxstudio.info) on the same host, list every consumer of laravel-lang/* packages in the org, rotate every CI secret in scope since 2026-05-22 22:32 UTC, and grep composer.lock fleet-wide for the article's imposter SHAs.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("systemd","init")
| where (FolderPath matches regex @"^/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}$")
   or (FileName matches regex @"^php[0-9]?$" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}(\.php)?")
   or (FolderPath startswith "/tmp/.laravel_locale")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, ProcessId, InitiatingProcessId
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("systemd","init") or ParentProcessId == 1
| where (ActingProcessName matches regex @"^/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}$")
   or (ActingProcessName endswith "/php" and ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}(\.php)?")
   or (ActingProcessName startswith "/tmp/.laravel_locale")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessId, ActingProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Orphaned PHP/ELF from /tmp Hidden Hex Path (Laravel-Lang Composer SC Stage-2)
id: 5e2c3d4f-6a7b-8c9d-0e1f-2a3b4c5d6e7f
description: Detects a process whose parent is systemd/init (reparented ppid=1) running from /tmp/.<hex> or whose command line references the Laravel-Lang stage-2 hidden dropper path. The article notes both an orphaned php and an unnamed ELF process executing from a now-deleted /tmp path.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:

  - attack.t1564.001
  - attack.t1070.004
  - attack.defense_evasion
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:

      - '/init'

  condition: selection_parent and selection_target
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.parent.name:systemd OR @process.parent.name:init OR @process.parent.pid:1) (@process.executable.path:/tmp/.* OR @process.command_line:*/tmp/.*)
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 OR #event_simpleName=SyntheticProcessRollup2) ParentBaseFileName=/^(systemd|init)$/i
| (regex("^/tmp/\\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}$", field=ImageFileName) OR regex("/tmp/\\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}(\\.php)?", field=CommandLine) OR regex("^/tmp/\\.laravel_locale/", field=ImageFileName))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("systemd","init") OR Processes.parent_process_id=1) AND (Processes.process_path="/tmp/.*" OR Processes.process="*/tmp/.*" OR Processes.process_name="php") by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.process_path, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.parent_process_id | `drop_dm_object_name("Processes")` | rex field=process_path "^/tmp/\.(?<hex_name>[a-f0-9]{6,12})$" | rex field=process "/tmp/\.(?<cmd_hex>[a-f0-9]{6,12})" | where isnotnull(hex_name) OR isnotnull(cmd_hex) | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("systemd","init") OR Processes.parent_process_id=1) AND (Processes.process_path="/tmp/.*" OR Processes.process="*/tmp/.*" OR Processes.process_name="php") by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.process_path, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.parent_process_id | `drop_dm_object_name("Processes")` | rex field=process_path "^/tmp/\.(?<hex_name>[a-f0-9]{6,12})$" | rex field=process "/tmp/\.(?<cmd_hex>[a-f0-9]{6,12})" | where isnotnull(hex_name) OR isnotnull(cmd_hex) | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
GitHub bulk git tag force-push by single actor across multiple org repos AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the org-wide tag-rewrite shape that defined the initial-access step: one GitHub actor force-pushing tags across multiple repositories in the same org within a short window (the Laravel-Lang attacker rewrote 502+ tags across four repos in 88 minutes). Combine with commit-author imposter signature 'Your Name' / 'you@example.com'. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact shape: 'every git tag across multiple popular Composer packages within a single 15 minute window', 502 tags rewritten in one repo, four repos hit in 88 minutes, all by the same compromised credential. The commit-author imposter strings 'Your Name' / 'you@example.com' are also called out verbatim. Sentinel/Defender/Falcon are left empty because GitHub audit telemetry is not in their canonical schemas — Splunk and Datadog (via the GitHub integration) are the realistic shipping paths.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1078 T1098
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Release engineer rewriting tags during a versioning-scheme migration (e.g. moving from 1.x.x to v1.x.x prefix)
  • Bot account (github-actions[bot], dependabot, release-please) performing org-wide tag housekeeping
  • Repository migration tool replaying tags after import from another VCS
  • Legitimate force-push after revoking an inadvertently-published tag pointing at a leaked secret
Suppression filter
| where actor != "github-actions[bot]" AND actor != "dependabot[bot]" AND actor !="release-please[bot]" AND NOT match(actor, "^.*\[bot\]$")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the actor account and the credential type (PAT, fine-grained PAT, OAuth app, GitHub App, SSH key); pull the actor's recent IP / user-agent history from GitHub audit and compare to known good. Check whether commits in the rewrite carry author identity 'Your Name <you@example.com>' — the campaign signature. 2) Contain: immediately revoke the actor's tokens/sessions and rotate the credential; enable tag protection and disable force-push to tags org-wide; restore tags from a known-good local clone or Packagist mirror SHA. 3) Hunt: search every org repo for commits authored by you@example.com; enumerate every consumer (downstream packages, internal Laravel apps) whose composer.lock points at one of the article's imposter SHAs (a5ea2e8f..., 50ac0db4..., bba2e443..., etc.); treat every CI secret accessible to consumers since 2026-05-22 22:32 UTC as compromised.
source:github (@action:git.push OR @action:git.create) @git.ref:refs/tags/*
CLOUD
index=* sourcetype IN ("github:audit","github_audit_log","github:enterprise:audit") (action="git.push" OR action="git.create" OR action="protected_branch.policy_override") ref="refs/tags/*"
| eval repo_org=mvindex(split(repo,"/"),0)
| stats min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen dc(repo) as repo_count dc(ref) as tag_count values(repo) as repos values(ref) as refs by actor, repo_org
| eval window_seconds = last_seen - first_seen
| where tag_count >= 10 AND repo_count >= 2 AND window_seconds <= 3600
| eval window_minutes = round(window_seconds/60, 1)
| convert ctime(first_seen) ctime(last_seen)
| sort - tag_count
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High

Nx Console v18.95.0 Malicious Payload Bootstrap via Orphan Commit (npx github:nrwl/nx#558b09d7) AIDelivery High
Detects the malicious Nx Console v18.95.0 workspace-activation bootstrap step — npx (or node) executing code fetched from the dangling orphan commit 558b09d7 on github.com/nrwl/nx, spawned by a VS Code-family editor (Code, Code-Insiders, Cursor, Codium). This is the exact in-the-wild payload-fetch string published by StepSecurity. Rationale: The orphan-commit ref `558b09d7` (full SHA 558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2) and the `nrwl/nx#558b09d7` npx fragment are unique strings published in the StepSecurity report and confirmed by The Hacker News, GBHackers, and Cyberpress — no legitimate Nx workflow targets this hash. Parent constraint on VS Code-family editors anchors the workspace-activation behaviour described in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://gbhackers.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension/ • https://cyberpress.org/nx-console-hijacked-attack/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher reproducing the IOC inside an isolated VM
  • SOC engineer red-team replay of the attack in a controlled exercise
  • Threat intel team triage downloading the orphan commit for malware analysis
  • Internal nrwl developer reproducing the issue for remediation work
  • Sandbox/CI job intentionally pulling the malicious commit for static analysis
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "sandbox" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "detonation" and DeviceName !startswith "sec-research-"
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: pull the device's recent process tree around the Timestamp — confirm parent is VS Code/Cursor and identify the user. Inspect the full ProcessCommandLine for `558b09d7` and confirm the npx call wasn't user-initiated. 2. CONTAIN: isolate the host via Defender Live Response or CrowdStrike Network Containment. Force the user to rotate GitHub PAT, npm token, AWS credentials, SSH keys, 1Password tokens, Vault tokens; revoke any OIDC tokens issued from CI for repos owned by this user. 3. HUNT: pivot on this DeviceId for `cat.py`, `kitty-monitor.plist`, `/tmp/kitty-*`, outbound to `169.254.169.254`, and any `api.github.com/search/commits?q=firedalazer` traffic. Sweep the org for `code --list-extensions` outputs containing `nrwl.angular-console@18.95.0` — every install of that exact version is presumed compromised.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("code.exe","code - insiders.exe","cursor.exe","codium.exe","vscodium.exe","electron","code helper","code","cursor","codium")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("github:nrwl/nx#558b09d7","nrwl/nx#558b09d7","558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("\\Code.exe","\\Code - Insiders.exe","\\Cursor.exe","\\Codium.exe","\\VSCodium.exe")
    | where CommandLine has_any ("github:nrwl/nx#558b09d7","nrwl/nx#558b09d7","558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine),
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("code","cursor","codium","Code Helper","Code - Insiders","Electron")
    | where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("github:nrwl/nx#558b09d7","nrwl/nx#558b09d7","558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, Account = ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName = TargetProcessName, CommandLine = TargetProcessCommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Nx Console v18.95.0 Compromised VSIX / main.js / payload SHA-256 Hash Match AIInstallation Medium
Detects file-system writes, process executions, or image loads matching any of the three SHA-256 hashes published by StepSecurity for the compromised Nx Console artefacts: the VSIX bundle, main.js, and the obfuscated index.js payload. Rationale: The three SHA-256 hashes are published verbatim in the StepSecurity post and corroborated by The Hacker News and GBHackers; a cryptographic hash match is the highest-fidelity primitive available. Hash collisions on SHA-256 are computationally infeasible — any hit on a non-sandbox host is a true positive. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://gbhackers.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware analyst opening the IOC sample on an instrumented VM
  • SOC threat-intel pipeline ingesting and storing the binary for retro-hunt
  • Yara/EDR signature self-test runs that reload sample binaries
  • Backup/restore of a known-bad VSIX file from quarantine for forensic review
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !startswith "sec-research-" and DeviceName !startswith "sandbox-" and FolderPath !has "\\Quarantine\\" and FolderPath !has "/quarantine/"
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: confirm hash hit is on a production endpoint, not the malware-analysis sandbox. Capture the file (DownloadFile / Live Response) and preserve for forensics; pull the surrounding 30 min of process events. 2. CONTAIN: network-isolate the device; quarantine the file via custom indicator block on the SHA-256 across the EDR fleet; force the user to rotate GitHub PAT, npm tokens, AWS keys, Kubernetes kubeconfig, 1Password session tokens, SSH keys, Vault tokens. 3. HUNT: org-wide retro-hunt for these three hashes across the past 30 days. Sweep CI/CD runners and developer laptops for `code --list-extensions --show-versions | grep angular-console` returning `18.95.0`. Audit recent npm publishes signed by org members for unexpected versions (the payload includes Sigstore forgery capability).
let MaliciousHashes = dynamic([
    "1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8",
    "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74",
    "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1"
]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where SHA256 in (MaliciousHashes) or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in (MaliciousHashes)
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Source="Process", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine),
    (DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where SHA256 in (MaliciousHashes)
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="FileWrite", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
    (DeviceImageLoadEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where SHA256 in (MaliciousHashes)
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="ImageLoad", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| order by Timestamp desc
let MaliciousHashes = dynamic([
    "1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8",
    "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74",
    "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1"
]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (SecurityEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where EventID == 4688
        | where FileHash in (MaliciousHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, FileHash),
    (ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in (MaliciousHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, NewProcessName=TargetFileName, CommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, FileHash=TargetFileSHA256),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where FileHash in (MaliciousHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, Account=SourceUserName, NewProcessName=SourceProcessName, CommandLine=RequestURL, FileHash)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

macOS LaunchAgent Persistence — com.user.kitty-monitor.plist (Nx Console Compromise) AIInstallation High
Detects creation of the LaunchAgent plist `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist` — the macOS persistence mechanism dropped by the Nx Console v18.95.0 obfuscated payload to keep the credential-stealer running across logins. Rationale: The exact filename `com.user.kitty-monitor.plist` under `~/Library/LaunchAgents/` is published in the StepSecurity IOC list and corroborated by The Hacker News write-up. It is a unique persistence artefact — no legitimate macOS software uses this bundle identifier — making any file-create event on this path a true positive. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://gbhackers.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension/
ATT&CKT1543.001 T1547
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR analyst copying the plist into a forensic evidence bag on a quarantine workstation
  • Sandbox environment intentionally executing the payload to capture the artefact
  • Threat-intel research team replaying the IOC for signature engineering
  • Backup software restoring a previously-captured LaunchAgents directory from snapshot
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !startswith "sec-ir-" and DeviceName !startswith "sandbox-" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "/quarantine/"
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: confirm the host is a real macOS endpoint (not a quarantine VM); read the plist contents — it should reference cat.py or a python interpreter pointing at the kitty backdoor. Identify the user owning ~/Library/LaunchAgents. 2. CONTAIN: `launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist`, delete the plist, kill any python process referencing `cat.py` or with `__DAEMONIZED=1` in its env, network-isolate the host. Rotate the user's GitHub PAT, npm token, AWS keys, SSH keys, 1Password tokens, Vault tokens. 3. HUNT: on the same host check for `~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py`, `/tmp/kitty-*`, `/var/tmp/.gh_update_state`, outbound to `169.254.169.254`, and the npx orphan-commit execution from UC1. Across the org, hunt for any other LaunchAgents with bundle id starting `com.user.kitty-*`.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has "/Library/LaunchAgents/" or FolderPath has @"\Library\LaunchAgents\"
| where FileName =~ "com.user.kitty-monitor.plist" or FolderPath endswith "com.user.kitty-monitor.plist"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileCreate")
| where TargetFilePath has "/Library/LaunchAgents/"
| where TargetFileName =~ "com.user.kitty-monitor.plist" or TargetFilePath endswith "com.user.kitty-monitor.plist"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, EventType, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Kitty cat.py Python Backdoor File Drop / Execution (Nx Console Compromise) AIInstallation High
Detects creation of `~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py` or execution of a python interpreter referencing that path or `/tmp/kitty-*` — the Linux/macOS Python backdoor stage dropped by the Nx Console v18.95.0 obfuscated payload. Rationale: The path `~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py` and `/tmp/kitty-*` directories are published verbatim in the StepSecurity IOC list and corroborated by The Hacker News and GBHackers. The `kitty` directory under user-local share is unrelated to the legitimate Kitty terminal (which uses `~/.config/kitty/`) — there is no benign use of this exact path, making it high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://gbhackers.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension/
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR analyst staging the artefact into evidence storage
  • Sandbox/research VM replaying the payload
  • Backup software restoring ~/.local/share contents from prior snapshot
  • Misconfigured tool dropping a stray cat.py under share/kitty (extremely rare — the legitimate Kitty terminal uses ~/.config/kitty/)
Suppression filter
| where ActingProcessName !has "forensic" and ActingProcessCommandLine !has "/evidence/" and DvcHostname !startswith "sec-ir-"
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: read cat.py contents (it should be obfuscated python). Identify the python parent process and the user. Look for an environment variable `__DAEMONIZED=1` on running python processes (article + external sources flag this as the daemonised state marker). 2. CONTAIN: `kill` any running python process referencing cat.py or with `__DAEMONIZED=1`; remove `~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py`, `/tmp/kitty-*`, `/var/tmp/.gh_update_state`, and the `com.user.kitty-monitor.plist` LaunchAgent. Network-isolate the host. Rotate credentials (GitHub, npm, AWS, 1Password, Vault, SSH). 3. HUNT: pivot on this DeviceId for outbound to `api.github.com/search/commits?q=firedalazer` and to `169.254.169.254`. Across the org, look for any python process with `__DAEMONIZED=1` set, or any cat.py outside legitimate repo locations.
union
  (DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
    | where (FolderPath has "/.local/share/kitty/" and FileName =~ "cat.py")
         or FolderPath matches regex @"^/tmp/kitty-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]+/"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="FileWrite", ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256),
  (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName has_any ("python","python3","python2") or InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","python3","python2")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (".local/share/kitty/cat.py","/kitty/cat.py","/tmp/kitty-")
         or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (".local/share/kitty/cat.py","/kitty/cat.py","/tmp/kitty-")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Source="Exec", ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine, SHA256)
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileCreate")
    | where (TargetFilePath has "/.local/share/kitty/" and TargetFileName =~ "cat.py")
         or TargetFilePath matches regex @"^/tmp/kitty-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]+/"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, Source="FileWrite", EventType, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256),
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where TargetProcessName has_any ("python","python3","python2")
    | where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (".local/share/kitty/cat.py","/kitty/cat.py","/tmp/kitty-")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, Source="Exec", EventType, TargetFileName=TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath=TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName=ParentProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine=TargetProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256=SHA256)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

AWS IMDS (169.254.169.254) Hit from Developer / Non-EC2 Endpoint (Nx Console Credential Theft) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects outbound connections to the AWS Instance Metadata Service (169.254.169.254) from endpoints that are not EC2 instances. The Nx Console v18.95.0 payload probes IMDS to steal IAM role credentials — a developer laptop or non-AWS workstation contacting IMDS is a strong credential-access signal. Rationale: The article and external corroboration (The Hacker News, CyberSecurityNews, GBHackers) call out `Connections to AWS IMDS (169.254.169.254) from non-AWS environments` as a documented IOC of the Nx Console payload's credential-stealing stage. The 169.254.169.254 link-local address has only one legitimate use (EC2/IMDS); any hit from a Mac/Linux laptop or developer workstation is anomalous. Sigma is omitted because the detection requires asset-class context (non-EC2) that single-event Sigma cannot express cleanly. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://cybersecuritynews.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised/ • https://gbhackers.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension/
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1078.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • EC2 instances onboarded to Defender/Sentinel/CrowdStrike where IMDS access is normal
  • Developer running aws-vault, aws sso login, or testing IMDSv2 emulators (e.g. amazon/amazon-ec2-metadata-mock) locally
  • CI runners self-hosted on EC2 that ship telemetry
  • Misconfigured Docker Desktop networking exposing the link-local address
  • Penetration testers running cloud-credential-extraction tools against test EC2s
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("aws.exe","aws","aws-vault.exe","aws-vault","awscli","amazon-ec2-metadata-mock") and DeviceCategory !in~ ("Server","Virtual Machine") and OSPlatform !startswith "WindowsServer"
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: confirm the source host is NOT an EC2 instance (check DeviceInfo.DeviceCategory, asset CMDB, public-IP geo). Identify the InitiatingProcessFileName — node/python/curl/wget from a developer workstation is high-signal; aws-vault / vscode / aws-cli is low-signal but still worth confirming. 2. CONTAIN: if non-EC2 + non-AWS-tooling process, network-isolate the host. Revoke any AWS access keys, session tokens, and assume-role credentials available to that user; force a workforce SSO re-auth. 3. HUNT: on the same host pivot to UC1 (npx orphan commit), UC3 (kitty-monitor.plist), UC4 (cat.py), and outbound to `api.github.com/search/commits?q=firedalazer`. Across CloudTrail, hunt for `AssumeRole` / `GetSessionToken` / `sts:GetCallerIdentity` from the user's AWS keys from non-corporate egress IPs in the past 7 days.
let DevEndpoints = DeviceInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, DeviceCategory, OSPlatform, DeviceType, IsInternetFacing) by DeviceId, DeviceName
    | where DeviceCategory != "Server" or isempty(DeviceCategory);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP == "169.254.169.254"
| where RemotePort in (80,443,8080)
| join kind=inner DevEndpoints on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, DeviceCategory, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr == "169.254.169.254"
| where DstPortNumber in (80,443,8080)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, NetworkApplicationProtocol, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkBytes, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd OR source:linux.syslog OR source:osquery) (@DestinationIp:169.254.169.254 OR @network.destination.ip:169.254.169.254 OR @DestinationHostname:*169.254.169.254*) -@host.tags:cloud_provider\:aws
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4="169.254.169.254" RemotePort=/^(80|443|8080)$/ | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count())

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"

| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"

| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__HASH_LIST__` placeholder with article-specific SHA256
    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:

ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

Operation FlutterBridge: macOS Malvertising Campaign Spreads New FlutterShell Backdoor

Unit 42 (Palo Alto)
2026-06-02 12 use cases 6 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Operation FlutterBridge is a malvertising campaign targeting macOS users. It distributed the new backdoor FlutterShell, built using the Flutter framework. The post Operation FlutterBridge: macOS Malvertising Campaign Spreads New FlutterShell Backdoor appeared first on Unit 42 .

ATT&CKT1027 T1176 T1190 T1555.003 T1574.002 T1649
Domainsatsheisdomestic.org etoftheappyrince.org healightejustb.org sinterfumesco.com ads-parkpro.com adsparkpro.top adsparkpro.net softwe.art
SHA256021666417de8b997… 363923500ce942bf… 8421c902364980e3… 644fc49fa1006a2a… 9053e8ddaecca1f9…

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] FlutterShell macOS payload SHA256 IOC match · Suspicious browser extension installation · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] FlutterShell macOS C2 contact (atsheisdomestic / etoftheappyrince / healightejustb) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Non-Chrome process modifies macOS Chrome Preferences (FlutterShell browser hijack) · [LLM] FlutterShell adware redirector contact (ads-parkpro / sinterfumesco / softwe.art) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
FlutterShell macOS C2 contact (atsheisdomestic / etoftheappyrince / healightejustb) AICommand & Control High
Detects endpoint contact to the three FlutterShell variant-specific C2 domains catalogued by Unit 42 for the PodcastsLounge, PDF-Brain, and PDF-Ninja variants. Hits represent post-installation backdoor check-in, not adware redirect. Rationale: Three C2 domains are listed in the Unit 42 variant matrix (Table 2) — single-purpose attacker infrastructure with no legitimate traffic; cross-checked against the Unit 42 report. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/flutterbridge-new-fluttershell-backdoor/ • https://cyberpress.org/jscorerunner-malware/ • https://gbhackers.com/new-mac-malware/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel analyst sandbox detonating the FlutterShell sample
  • DFIR responder validating IOC scope after acknowledged incident
  • TI feed health-check pollers (e.g. MISP, OTX) resolving the domain
  • DNS sinkhole / RPZ logging the redirected query
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("sandbox-exec","VirusTotalUploader","misp-modules")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating process, signing identity, and full installer path on the macOS host — confirm it is PodcastsLounge.app, PDF-Brain.app, PDF-Ninja.app, or another Flutter-built app under /Applications. Pull SHA256 and check against the 8 Unit 42 hashes. 2) Contain: isolate the macOS host via Defender XDR or MDM, kill the Flutter binary, quarantine the .app bundle, and revoke the Apple Developer ID team if the bundle is signed (notify Apple via Developer feedback). 3) Hunt: pivot on the device's last 30 days of DNS to the other two variant C2 domains plus the five adware redirector domains; query DeviceFileEvents for modifications to ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Preferences and Secure Preferences by the same parent.
let C2 = dynamic(["atsheisdomestic.org","etoftheappyrince.org","healightejustb.org"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (C2) or RemoteUrl endswith ".atsheisdomestic.org" or RemoteUrl endswith ".etoftheappyrince.org" or RemoteUrl endswith ".healightejustb.org"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let C2 = dynamic(["atsheisdomestic.org","etoftheappyrince.org","healightejustb.org"]);
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery has_any (C2)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName, EventVendor, EventProduct
| union (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Url has_any (C2) or HttpHostName has_any (C2)
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery=HttpHostName, DnsResponseName=Url, EventVendor, EventProduct)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

FlutterShell macOS payload SHA256 IOC match AIInstallation Medium
Hashes any binary write or execution against the 8 SHA256 indicators Unit 42 published for the three FlutterShell variant builds. Catches the malware itself regardless of bundle name, since the actor has signed multiple Developer ID identities. Rationale: Eight SHA256s explicitly published by Unit 42 across PodcastsLounge, PDF-Brain, and PDF-Ninja variants. Hash IOC matching has near-zero FP outside of analyst sandboxes — high alerting fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/flutterbridge-new-fluttershell-backdoor/
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1036.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel analyst detonating sample in macOS sandbox
  • Reverse-engineering team copying binary onto research host
  • EDR scheduled scan during initial IOC ingestion (telemetry replay)
  • TI platform downloading sample for hashing
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !in ("SOC-MAL-LAB-01","IR-DETONATION-MAC")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm which variant by hash (Unit 42 Table 2 ties each hash family to PodcastsLounge / PDF-Brain / PDF-Ninja), pull the .app bundle path, and capture the Developer ID Team Identifier from the codesign data — Apple will need it to revoke. 2) Contain: isolate device, kill the parent Flutter binary, quarantine the .app bundle, and use `spctl --remove` plus `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine` history to confirm Gatekeeper assessment. Block hashes at MDR / Defender ASR. 3) Hunt: search the FileOriginUrl on DeviceFileEvents for the Google Ads landing path to map other users who clicked the same malvertising lure; pivot upstream on the served domain.

Non-Chrome process modifies macOS Chrome Preferences (FlutterShell browser hijack) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Catches the FlutterShell adware stage where the malware rewrites ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Preferences (and Secure Preferences / Local State) to force traffic through the attacker-controlled redirector. Chrome itself is the only normal writer of these files on macOS. Rationale: Article explicitly states FlutterShell 'modifies Google Chrome configuration files to hijack the browser' — the three macOS Chrome state files are the documented hijack targets and Chrome itself is the only normal writer. Pivoting on InitiatingProcessFileName surfaces the Flutter binary by name. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/flutterbridge-new-fluttershell-backdoor/
ATT&CKT1176 T1539 T1185
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Jamf/Intune/Workspace ONE pushing Chrome managed-preference plist
  • User running a Chrome profile reset utility (e.g. CleanMyMac, Onyx)
  • Chrome Beta/Canary side-by-side install writing the same path
  • Engineering team using `defaults` CLI for profile automation
  • Backup software (Time Machine, Backblaze) writing restore copies
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !contains "jamf" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !contains "Intune" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("managedsoftwareupdate","munki","profiles")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the modifying process SHA256 and parent — confirm whether it's a Flutter-built signed app (look for `Flutter.framework` inside the .app bundle and `--obfuscate` in libapp.dylib symbols). Diff the Preferences JSON against a known-good baseline to find the injected default_search_provider / homepage / startup URL. 2) Contain: revert Preferences/Secure Preferences/Local State from Time Machine or to defaults; isolate the host; quarantine the parent .app bundle. 3) Hunt: pivot on the same InitiatingProcessSHA256 across the fleet, and search DeviceNetworkEvents for contact to ads-parkpro.com / adsparkpro.top / adsparkpro.net / sinterfumesco.com / softwe.art for any other hosts whose Chrome was hijacked.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FolderPath contains "/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/"
| where FileName in ("Preferences","Secure Preferences","Local State")
| where ActionType in ("FileModified","FileCreated")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("Google Chrome","Google Chrome Helper","Google Chrome Helper (Renderer)","Google Chrome Helper (GPU)","chrome","chrome_crashpad_handler")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !contains "jamf" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !contains "intune" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("managedsoftwareupdate","munki")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where TargetFilePath has "/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/"
| where TargetFileName in ("Preferences","Secure Preferences","Local State")
| where EventType in ("FileModified","FileCreated","FileWritten")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("Google Chrome","Google Chrome Helper","Google Chrome Helper (Renderer)","Google Chrome Helper (GPU)","chrome","chrome_crashpad_handler")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine !contains "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256, EventVendor, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Non-Chrome Process Writing macOS Chrome Preferences (FlutterShell Browser Hijack)
id: 2c5e9a13-b6f4-49d2-9e8b-4f2a1c7d3b08
description: Detects modification of Google Chrome Preferences / Secure Preferences / Local State on macOS by a process other than Chrome itself. FlutterShell rewrites these files to force browser traffic through ads-parkpro / softwe.art redirectors.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/flutterbridge-new-fluttershell-backdoor/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/02
tags:
  - attack.t1176
  - attack.t1185
  - attack.t1539
  - attack.impact
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: macos
detection:
  target_files:
    TargetFilename|contains: '/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/'
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '/Preferences'
      - '/Secure Preferences'
      - '/Local State'
  filter_chrome:
    Image|contains: '/Google Chrome.app/Contents/'
  condition: target_files and not filter_chrome
falsepositives:
  - MDM-pushed Chrome enterprise policy writes (Jamf, Intune, Workspace ONE)
  - User-driven Chrome profile reset utilities
level: medium
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| regex("/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/", field=TargetFileName)
| TargetFileName=/(Preferences|Secure Preferences|Local State)$/
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/\/Google Chrome\.app\/Contents\/.+\/(Google Chrome|Google Chrome Helper.*|chrome_crashpad_handler|chrome)$/)
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/(jamf|munki|managedsoftwareupdate|intune)/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=[count(), min(@timestamp), max(@timestamp)])
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc values(Filesystem.process_path) as proc_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="*/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/*" (Filesystem.file_name="Preferences" OR Filesystem.file_name="Secure Preferences" OR Filesystem.file_name="Local State") NOT (Filesystem.process_name IN ("Google Chrome","Google Chrome Helper","Google Chrome Helper (Renderer)","chrome","chrome_crashpad_handler")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name host | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc values(Filesystem.process_path) as proc_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="*/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/*" (Filesystem.file_name="Preferences" OR Filesystem.file_name="Secure Preferences" OR Filesystem.file_name="Local State") NOT (Filesystem.process_name IN ("Google Chrome","Google Chrome Helper","Google Chrome Helper (Renderer)","chrome","chrome_crashpad_handler")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name host | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
FlutterShell adware redirector contact (ads-parkpro / sinterfumesco / softwe.art) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects endpoint contact to the five adware-redirector domains the FlutterShell campaign funnels hijacked browser traffic through. Distinct from the C2 detection — these surface the in-the-wild adware stage and may catch hosts where the C2 has rotated. Rationale: Five redirector domains listed in the Unit 42 IOC bundle as the ad-filled intermediary destinations. Catching them complements the C2 detection (which fires post-install) by catching the visible browser-hijack symptom, which often persists even after the C2 rotates. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/flutterbridge-new-fluttershell-backdoor/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1583.008
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • URL-reputation scanner (URLScan, VirusTotal, Quad9) probing the redirector
  • SOC analyst opening the IOC in a sandbox browser
  • Web filtering vendor crawler categorising the domain
  • Email security solution detonating a URL containing the redirector
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("URLScan","safe_browsing","webroot") and DeviceName !startswith "SOC-"
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating browser process and check whether the host also resolved any of the three FlutterShell C2 domains in the last 30 days — joint signal raises this from adware-noise to FlutterShell install. Diff Chrome Preferences against baseline. 2) Contain: block the five domains at SWG/proxy and EDR network indicators; reset the user's Chrome profile; isolate if joint with C2 hits or hash hits. 3) Hunt: pivot on the .app bundle Developer ID Team Identifier across the macOS fleet for other notarised apps from the same signer that may not yet have a hash IOC; review Google Ads click telemetry (UrlClickEvents) for the lure URL upstream.
let Redirectors = dynamic(["sinterfumesco.com","ads-parkpro.com","adsparkpro.top","adsparkpro.net","softwe.art"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (Redirectors)
   or RemoteUrl endswith ".sinterfumesco.com"
   or RemoteUrl endswith ".ads-parkpro.com"
   or RemoteUrl endswith ".adsparkpro.top"
   or RemoteUrl endswith ".adsparkpro.net"
   or RemoteUrl endswith ".softwe.art"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let Redirectors = dynamic(["sinterfumesco.com","ads-parkpro.com","adsparkpro.top","adsparkpro.net","softwe.art"]);
let dnsHits = ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (Redirectors)
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, Url=DnsQuery, EventVendor, EventProduct;
let webHits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Url has_any (Redirectors) or HttpHostName has_any (Redirectors)
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, EventVendor, EventProduct;
union dnsHits, webHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: FlutterShell macOS Adware Redirector Domain Contact
id: 9d2e4b1c-7a83-4c6f-be21-3f9a8e2d5b41
description: Detects DNS/HTTP contact to the five adware redirector domains operated by the Operation FlutterBridge actor — the post-hijack stage that forces all Chrome traffic through attacker infrastructure.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/flutterbridge-new-fluttershell-backdoor/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/02
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1583.008
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|endswith:
      - 'sinterfumesco.com'
      - 'ads-parkpro.com'
      - 'adsparkpro.top'
      - 'adsparkpro.net'
      - 'softwe.art'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - URL-reputation crawlers visiting the redirector
level: high
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| DomainName=/(^|\.)(sinterfumesco\.com|ads-parkpro\.com|adsparkpro\.top|adsparkpro\.net|softwe\.art)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=[count(), min(@timestamp), max(@timestamp)])
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.src) as src values(All_Traffic.app) as app from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_host IN ("sinterfumesco.com","ads-parkpro.com","adsparkpro.top","adsparkpro.net","softwe.art","*.sinterfumesco.com","*.ads-parkpro.com","*.adsparkpro.top","*.adsparkpro.net","*.softwe.art") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest_host All_Traffic.user host | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | appendpipe [| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.url IN ("*sinterfumesco.com*","*ads-parkpro.com*","*adsparkpro.top*","*adsparkpro.net*","*softwe.art*") by Web.src Web.url Web.http_referrer host | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.src) as src values(All_Traffic.app) as app from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_host IN ("sinterfumesco.com","ads-parkpro.com","adsparkpro.top","adsparkpro.net","softwe.art","*.sinterfumesco.com","*.ads-parkpro.com","*.adsparkpro.top","*.adsparkpro.net","*.softwe.art") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest_host All_Traffic.user host | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | appendpipe [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.url IN ("*sinterfumesco.com*","*ads-parkpro.com*","*adsparkpro.top*","*adsparkpro.net*","*softwe.art*") by Web.src Web.url Web.http_referrer host | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("atsheisdomestic.org", "etoftheappyrince.org", "healightejustb.org", "sinterfumesco.com", "ads-parkpro.com", "adsparkpro.top", "adsparkpro.net", "softwe.art")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["atsheisdomestic.org", "etoftheappyrince.org", "healightejustb.org", "sinterfumesco.com", "ads-parkpro.com", "adsparkpro.top", "adsparkpro.net", "softwe.art"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc
