node child of npm install initiating outbound network to non-registry destination AICommand & Control Medium
Surfaces the Miasma exfiltration step: a node.exe spawned by npm/yarn/pnpm/npx during install opens an outbound socket to anything other than the npm registry, yarn registry, github.com or githubusercontent.com. Honest preinstall scripts almost never call out to arbitrary internet hosts. Rationale: Article describes a 4.2 MB obfuscated payload that exfiltrates harvested secrets — exfiltration must traverse the network, and a clean npm preinstall should only ever talk to the registry/GitHub. Joining the network event back to a node-under-npm process tree via host + PID + 10-minute window is the cleanest way to attribute. Sentinel side joins ImNetworkSession to ImProcessCreate on host + time (ImNetworkSession has no process-name column, so attribution lives in the join, not in a direct field).
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001 T1567
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • node-gyp / native-module install pulling binaries from a vendor CDN (electron, sharp, node-sass) — add the specific CDN host to the allowlist after triage
  • Telemetry / analytics packages (e.g. typescript-language-server hitting an update channel) calling home during postinstall
  • Internal artifact mirror not yet added to the allowlist
  • CI builds that call a Slack webhook from a postinstall hook to notify the team
Suppression filter
| where not (DstHostname has_any ("electronjs.org", "sentry.io", "playwright.dev", "puppeteer.dev", "cypress.io") or RemoteUrl has_any ("electronjs.org", "sentry.io", "playwright.dev", "puppeteer.dev", "cypress.io"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: WHOIS/passive-DNS the destination; if it's a known CDN for a legit native-module install, add to the allowlist and re-run the hunt. 2) Contain: if the destination is unknown / newly registered, isolate the host or CI runner immediately and treat all secrets reachable from that build context as leaked. Block the destination at egress. 3) Hunt: pivot on the destination across the org (every host that beaconed) and on the source npm/yarn/pnpm install command to see which dependency triggered it — that's the candidate compromised package.
let NpmNodeProcs = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","npm","yarn","yarn.cmd","pnpm","pnpm.cmd","npx","npx.cmd","corepack.exe","corepack")
    | project NodeStart = Timestamp, DeviceId, NodePid = ProcessId, NodeCmd = ProcessCommandLine, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where not(RemoteUrl endswith "registry.npmjs.org"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "registry.yarnpkg.com"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "registry.npmmirror.com"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "github.com"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "githubusercontent.com"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "githubapp.com"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "objects.githubusercontent.com"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "nodejs.org"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "pypi.org"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "repo.maven.apache.org")
| join kind=inner NpmNodeProcs on $left.DeviceId == $right.DeviceId, $left.InitiatingProcessId == $right.NodePid
| where Timestamp between (NodeStart .. NodeStart + 10m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, NodeCmd, ParentCmd, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let NodeProcs = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActingProcessName endswith "node.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "/node" or ActingProcessName =~ "node"
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","npm","yarn.cmd","yarn","pnpm.cmd","pnpm","npx.cmd","npx","corepack")
    | project NodeHost = DvcHostname, NodeStart = EventStartTime, NodeCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentCmd = ParentProcessCommandLine;
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where NetworkDirection == "Outbound"
| where isnotempty(DstHostname)
| where not(DstHostname endswith "registry.npmjs.org"
        or DstHostname endswith "registry.yarnpkg.com"
        or DstHostname endswith "registry.npmmirror.com"
        or DstHostname endswith "github.com"
        or DstHostname endswith "githubusercontent.com"
        or DstHostname endswith "githubapp.com"
        or DstHostname endswith "nodejs.org"
        or DstHostname endswith "pypi.org"
        or DstHostname endswith "repo.maven.apache.org")
| join kind=inner NodeProcs on $left.SrcHostname == $right.NodeHost
| where TimeGenerated between (NodeStart .. NodeStart + 10m)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, NodeCmd, ParentCmd, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkBytes
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 (@Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE) OR @process.name:node) -@DestinationHostname:*.npmjs.org -@DestinationHostname:*.yarnpkg.com -@DestinationHostname:*.npmmirror.com -@DestinationHostname:*.github.com -@DestinationHostname:*.githubusercontent.com -@DestinationHostname:*.githubapp.com -@DestinationHostname:*.nodejs.org -@DestinationHostname:*.pypi.org -@DestinationHostname:*.maven.apache.org -CIDR(@DestinationIp, 10.0.0.0/8) -CIDR(@DestinationIp, 172.16.0.0/12) -CIDR(@DestinationIp, 192.168.0.0/16)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest ContextImageFileName=/\\node(\.exe)?$/i NOT (DomainName=/(\.|^)(registry\.npmjs\.org|registry\.yarnpkg\.com|registry\.npmmirror\.com|github\.com|githubusercontent\.com|githubapp\.com|nodejs\.org|pypi\.org|maven\.apache\.org)$/i)
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\node(\.exe)?$/i ParentBaseFileName=/^(npm(\.cmd|\.exe)?|yarn(\.cmd)?|pnpm(\.cmd)?|npx(\.cmd)?|corepack(\.exe)?)$/i | rename(field=TargetProcessId, as=NodePid)}, field=[aid, ContextProcessId], key=[aid, NodePid])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.app IN ("node.exe","node") OR All_Traffic.process_name IN ("node.exe","node")) AND All_Traffic.dest_port IN (80,443,8080,8443) AND All_Traffic.transport="tcp" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port _time

| where NOT match(dest, "(?i)(^|\.)(registry\.npmjs\.org|registry\.yarnpkg\.com|registry\.npmmirror\.com|github\.com|githubusercontent\.com|githubapp\.com|objects\.githubusercontent\.com|nodejs\.org|repo\.maven\.apache\.org|pypi\.org)$")
| join type=inner src [| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("node.exe","node") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","npm","yarn","yarn.cmd","pnpm","pnpm.cmd","npx","npx.cmd","corepack.exe","corepack") by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process Processes.process _time | rename Processes.dest as src, Processes.parent_process as parent_cmd, Processes.process as node_cmd, _time as node_start | eval node_end = node_start + 600]

| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.app IN ("node.exe","node") OR All_Traffic.process_name IN ("node.exe","node")) AND All_Traffic.dest_port IN (80,443,8080,8443) AND All_Traffic.transport="tcp" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port _time
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

| join type=inner src [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("node.exe","node") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","npm","yarn","yarn.cmd","pnpm","pnpm.cmd","npx","npx.cmd","corepack.exe","corepack") by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process Processes.process _time | rename Processes.dest as src, Processes.parent_process as parent_cmd, Processes.process as node_cmd, _time as node_start | eval node_end = node_start + 600]
| where _time >= node_start AND _time <= node_end

Install or update of @redhat-cloud-services npm package post-2026-06-01 (IOC version watchlist) AIDelivery Medium
File-event hunt for write activity under any node_modules\@redhat-cloud-services\<pkg>\ path on or after 2026-06-01. The runbook then reconciles the package version against the 30 IOC versions enumerated in the Aikido article — that step is too brittle for a single query but the file-write is a clean pivot point. Rationale: All 30 affected package names come straight from the IOC list in the article and the @redhat-cloud-services scope appears verbatim in Code Blocks 1 and 2. Date filter (>= 2026-06-01) matches the published compromise date. Version still needs runbook reconciliation because Defender/Sysmon/auditd file-event records don't expose package.json contents — the rationale is to give analysts a pivot, not a verdict.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Clean install of a post-rollback version of an affected package (Red Hat will publish patched releases) — runbook step 1 checks the version
  • Developer cloning a long-lived repo whose lockfile pins a clean pre-2026-06-01 version — file mtime reflects checkout time but contents are clean
  • CI build cache being warmed with a known-good tarball
  • Researcher reproducing the IOC in a sandbox VM that ships telemetry
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the package.json that was just written and confirm whether the version matches one of the 30 IOC versions in the article. If not affected, drop. 2) Contain: if affected, isolate the host or CI runner, kill node, and treat every secret class listed by Aikido (GITHUB_TOKEN, ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN, AWS, GCP, Azure SP, Vault, kubeconfig, npm/PyPI tokens, SSH, Docker, GPG, .env) as compromised — rotate before reuse. 3) Hunt: pivot the npm registry audit logs for any `publish` events from the same NPM_TOKEN since the install; check GitHub Actions run logs on this host's repos for jobs that may have used OIDC to push backdoored versions onward (the worm-spread leg).
let IOCPackages = dynamic(["chrome","compliance-client","config-manager-client","entitlements-client","eslint-config-redhat-cloud-services","frontend-components","frontend-components-advisor-components","frontend-components-config","frontend-components-config-utilities","frontend-components-notifications","frontend-components-remediations","frontend-components-testing","frontend-components-translations","frontend-components-utilities","hcc-feo-mcp","hcc-kessel-mcp","hcc-pf-mcp","host-inventory-client","insights-client","integrations-client","javascript-clients-shared","notifications-client","patch-client","quickstarts-client","rbac-client","remediations-client","rule-components","sources-client","tsc-transform-imports","types","vulnerabilities-client"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp >= datetime(2026-06-01T00:00:00Z)
| where FolderPath has "node_modules" and FolderPath has "@redhat-cloud-services"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| extend Pkg = extract(@"(?i)@redhat-cloud-services[\\/]([^\\/]+)", 1, FolderPath)
| where Pkg in~ (IOCPackages) or isempty(Pkg) == false
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), FileCount = count(), SampleFiles = make_set(strcat(FolderPath, "\\", FileName), 10) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, Pkg
| order by FirstSeen desc
let IOCPackages = dynamic(["chrome","compliance-client","config-manager-client","entitlements-client","eslint-config-redhat-cloud-services","frontend-components","frontend-components-advisor-components","frontend-components-config","frontend-components-config-utilities","frontend-components-notifications","frontend-components-remediations","frontend-components-testing","frontend-components-translations","frontend-components-utilities","hcc-feo-mcp","hcc-kessel-mcp","hcc-pf-mcp","host-inventory-client","insights-client","integrations-client","javascript-clients-shared","notifications-client","patch-client","quickstarts-client","rbac-client","remediations-client","rule-components","sources-client","tsc-transform-imports","types","vulnerabilities-client"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated >= datetime(2026-06-01T00:00:00Z)
| where TargetFilePath has "node_modules" and TargetFilePath has "@redhat-cloud-services"
| where EventType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileCreate","FileWrite")
| extend Pkg = extract(@"(?i)@redhat-cloud-services[\\/]([^\\/]+)", 1, TargetFilePath)
| where Pkg in~ (IOCPackages)
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), FileCount = count(), SampleFiles = make_set(TargetFilePath, 10) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, Pkg
| order by FirstSeen desc

Side-loaded / unsigned extensions, often masquerading as wallets, productivity tools.

| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or SHA1 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or MD5 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or SHA1 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or MD5 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: PATCH /workspaces/{id}/members/{user_id} role-change request AIExploitation High
Hunts the core privilege-escalation primitive in CVE-2026-47416 — an HTTP PATCH against /workspaces/<workspace_id>/members/<user_id> on praisonai-platform <=0.1.2. Because require_workspace_member defaults to min_role='member' and the route never overrides it, any authenticated member can write {"role":"owner"} to any member row. Outside of one-off legitimate owner-driven role tweaks this URL+verb pair is extremely rare, so even URI-only telemetry is high-fidelity for affected deployments. Rationale: Article pinpoints the exact endpoint shape (PATCH /workspaces/{workspace_id}/members/{user_id}) and the route file (api/routes/workspaces.py:115-127). Even without request-body visibility, the verb+path pair is rare enough on praisonai-platform to be high-fidelity; restricting on HTTP 2xx removes 401/403 noise from unaffected versions. Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory body and corroborated by independent PraisonAI security coverage on cybersecuritynews.com and Sysdig confirming the platform's pattern of weakly-gated workspace endpoints. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c2m8-4gcg-v22g • https://cybersecuritynews.com/praisonai-vulnerability-exploited/ • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/cve-2026-44338-praisonai-authentication-bypass-in-under-4-hours-and-the-growing-trend-of-rapid-exploitation
ATT&CKT1068 T1190 T1098
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate workspace owner promoting a new admin via the official praisonai-platform UI (verifiable by the actor already holding owner role pre-request)
  • Internal SRE tenant-provisioning script that bootstraps owner accounts on workspace creation
  • Patched 0.1.3+ deployments where the route now enforces min_role='owner' — successful PATCH events are by-design owner-driven
  • Synthetic monitoring / API probe pinging the endpoint as a uptime check
Suppression filter
// Refine by excluding sessions whose caller was already owner (requires JWT decode or join to membership audit):
// | where SrcUsername !in (toscalar(MembershipAuditLog | where Role == "owner" | summarize make_set(UserId)))
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the source IP, JWT subject, and User-Agent from the matching PATCH. Decode the JWT (or query the praisonai member table) to determine the caller's role at PATCH-time AND the target user_id from the URL path — if caller_role!=owner OR caller_id==target_id, treat as confirmed exploitation. 2. Contain: rotate the attacker JWT (revoke session), revert the modified member row to its pre-PATCH role from DB audit, force-rotate all owner credentials in the affected workspace, and block the source IP at the edge. 3. Hunt: enumerate every PATCH /workspaces/*/members/* in the last 30 days, list workspaces where >1 owner was added in a 1h window, and pull GET /auth/me + DELETE /workspaces/* requests from the same session for impact assessment.
// Primary: ASIM web session view (portable across nginx / IIS / App Gateway shippers).
let Lookback = 7d;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where HttpMethod =~ "PATCH"
| where Url matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/[^/?#]+"
| where HttpStatusCode in ("200","204")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, HttpMethod, Url, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestBodyBytes, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, DstHostname
| order by TimeGenerated desc
// Fallback for tenants shipping raw IIS:
// W3CIISLog
// | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
// | where csMethod =~ "PATCH"
// | where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/[^/?#]+"
// | where scStatus in ("200","204")
// | project TimeGenerated, cIP, csUserName, csMethod, csUriStem, scStatus, csUserAgent, Computer
title: praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416 PATCH workspaces members role-change
id: 7a4cbf8e-2b39-4b9a-a4ba-2026474160c1
status: experimental
description: Detects HTTP PATCH requests against the praisonai-platform /workspaces/{workspace_id}/members/{user_id} endpoint that exposes a vertical privilege-escalation primitive (CVE-2026-47416). The endpoint should normally see near-zero PATCH traffic; any successful PATCH is suspicious until the deployment is patched to >=0.1.3 with the min_role='owner' gate applied.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c2m8-4gcg-v22g
author: SOC Detection Engineering

    cs-method: 'PATCH'
  selection_uri:

  selection_status:
    sc-status:
      - 200
      - 204
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate workspace owner changing another member's role via the official UI (will be rare and identifiable by the originating account being an existing owner)
  - Internal admin scripts that pre-seed workspace ownership during tenant provisioning
level: high

praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: Member self-promotion + legitimate-owner demotion chain within one hour AIInstallation High
Catches the two-request takeover chain described in the advisory — the attacker first self-promotes (PATCH on their own user_id with {"role":"owner"}) and then demotes the legitimate owner (PATCH on the owner's user_id with {"role":"member"}). This temporal pivot is much higher fidelity than UC1 because legitimate workspace operations almost never produce two role-mutating PATCHs from the same client IP within a short window. Rationale: The advisory explicitly calls out the two-PATCH primitive: 'owner lockout in two requests total'. Workspaces where the same client IP/user mutates 2+ distinct member rows within the hour is a behaviour the legitimate UI essentially never produces — owners normally change one role at a time and rarely demote themselves seconds after promoting. Threshold of >=2 distinct TargetUser within 60m is the article's own attack cadence. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c2m8-4gcg-v22g
ATT&CKT1098 T1531 T1136.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Tenant migration script that bulk-rewrites member roles during a planned ownership handover
  • Initial workspace seeding when an org provisions one workspace with several pre-assigned owner+admin rows
  • Pen-test or red-team engagement that intentionally chains the exact takeover sequence (whitelist by source IP)
  • Internal QA replaying the advisory PoC in a non-prod tenant
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull every matching workspace_id and TargetUser pair from the alert window; compare against the pre-window state of the workspace_members table to identify who got promoted and who got demoted. 2. Contain: in the affected workspace immediately freeze role mutations (DB-level), revoke every JWT issued to any account whose role changed in the window, and restore the original owner from audit history. 3. Hunt: pivot on the SrcIpAddr / JWT subject across all workspaces (a single attacker may have pwned several tenants), and check for subsequent DELETE /workspaces/* or PATCH on settings to gauge data destruction risk.
let Lookback = 7d;
let WindowMin = 60m;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where HttpMethod =~ "PATCH"
| where Url matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/[^/?#]+"
| where HttpStatusCode in ("200","204")
| extend Workspace = extract(@"(?i)/workspaces/([^/]+)/members/", 1, Url)
| extend TargetUser = extract(@"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/([^/?#]+)", 1, Url)
| summarize PatchCount = count(),
            TargetsTouched = dcount(TargetUser),
            Targets = make_set(TargetUser, 10),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Workspace, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where PatchCount >= 2 and TargetsTouched >= 2   // self-promote + owner-demote = 2 distinct user_ids
| extend WindowMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| order by FirstSeen desc
@http.method:PATCH @http.url_details.path:*/workspaces/*/members/* @http.status_code:(200 OR 204) (service:praisonai-platform OR service:praisonai OR @service:praisonai*)

praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: Bulk agent/issue/project/comment enumeration immediately after a workspace role-change PATCH AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the collection phase of the takeover chain — once the attacker holds owner via the CVE-2026-47416 primitive they pivot into LIST endpoints (agents, issues, projects, comments) that were previously gated by owner-tier access. The detection joins a successful PATCH on /workspaces/*/members/* with a burst of GET/LIST traffic from the same session within 15 minutes, flagging the post-elevation data harvest. Rationale: Article explicitly chains the elevation into 'exfiltrate everything via the agent/issue/project/comment IDORs that were filed as separate advisories'. The named LIST endpoints come from the advisory's own corroboration section. Pairing the elevation event with the post-elevation enumeration inside 15 minutes weeds out generic browse traffic from a non-attack owner. Burst threshold of 10 distinct GETs is calibrated to the article's described mass-pull behaviour rather than a casual single-resource read. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c2m8-4gcg-v22g
ATT&CKT1213 T1530 T1087.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • New workspace owner doing a legitimate post-handover walkthrough of agents/issues/projects/comments
  • CI/CD or backup integration that lists workspace contents after permission changes (filter by service-account UA)
  • Internal admin auditing a workspace after a customer-support ticket
  • praisonai-platform UI dashboard that pre-fetches all four resource types on owner login (verify by tracing first-party UA + Referer)
Suppression filter
// Suppress first-party praisonai-platform UI pre-fetch by excluding the known UI Referer (configure per deployment):
// | where HttpRequestHeaderReferer !contains "/dashboard" or HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent !contains "praisonai-ui"
Response runbook
1. Triage: enumerate the exact resource IDs read (agent_ids, issue_ids, project_ids, comment_ids) in the burst window — these are the candidate exfil set. Pull the JWT subject to confirm whether the caller was a legitimate pre-existing owner or a freshly-elevated member. 2. Contain: revoke the session, rotate any API keys / secrets referenced inside the harvested agents (often the highest-value secondary impact — agent configs leak provider tokens), and notify data-owner for the affected resources. 3. Hunt: search outbound traffic from the attacker IP for any S3/object-store / paste-site uploads in the 30 minutes following the harvest, and check whether the same SrcIpAddr touched the companion delete_workspace endpoint.
let Lookback = 7d;
let PostWindow = 15m;
let BurstThreshold = 10;   // 10+ list calls inside 15m post-PATCH = harvest-shaped
let RoleChanges = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where HttpMethod =~ "PATCH"
    | where Url matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/[^/?#]+"
    | where HttpStatusCode in ("200","204")
    | project PatchTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, PatchedWorkspace = extract(@"(?i)/workspaces/([^/]+)/members/", 1, Url);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where HttpMethod =~ "GET"
| where Url matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/(agents|issues|projects|comments)"
| join kind=inner RoleChanges on SrcIpAddr
| where TimeGenerated between (PatchTime .. PatchTime + PostWindow)
| summarize ListCount = count(),
            DistinctResources = dcount(extract(@"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/(agents|issues|projects|comments)", 1, Url)),
            ListUrls = make_set(Url, 25),
            FirstList = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastList = max(TimeGenerated)
            by SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, PatchedWorkspace, PatchTime
| where ListCount >= BurstThreshold
| extend DelaySeconds = datetime_diff('second', FirstList, PatchTime)
| order by PatchTime desc

Vulnerable praisonai-platform deployment hunt (uvicorn launching praisonai_platform.api.app) AIInstallation High
Surfaces hosts running praisonai-platform — the vulnerable component in CVE-2026-47410. Defaults bypass the secret-guard when PLATFORM_ENV is unset (its default is 'dev'), so any deployment started without explicitly exporting PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET is exploitable. This UC identifies the population that needs urgent remediation before attackers find them on Shodan. Rationale: Pivots on the exact startup invocation named in the advisory (`uvicorn praisonai_platform.api.app:app`) and the package import name. The `--reload` exclusion drops developer workstations where the dev server is intentional. The SecretInCmdLine/ProdEnvInCmdLine extends help the analyst decide remediation urgency at triage time without a second query.
ATT&CKT1190 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer workstation running the platform locally with --reload (excluded by filter)
  • CI/CD runner executing integration tests against a throwaway praisonai_platform instance
  • Sanctioned production deployment that exports PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET via systemd EnvironmentFile (not visible in cmdline) — needs out-of-band verification
  • Container orchestrator (k8s, ECS) where the cmdline is the entrypoint and env is injected from a Secret/Parameter Store
  • Internal demo/lab box intentionally running on default secret
Suppression filter
and not (ProcessCommandLine has "--reload") and not (ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET\s*=\s*[^d ]") and not (DeviceName matches regex @"(?i)^(dev|tst|lab|ci|build)\-")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): For each hit, confirm whether PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET is actually set in the running process environment, not just the cmdline. On Linux: `sudo cat /proc/$PID/environ | tr '\0' '\n' | grep -E 'PLATFORM_(JWT_SECRET|ENV)'`. If JWT_SECRET is unset OR equals 'dev-secret-change-me' AND PLATFORM_ENV is unset/'dev', the host is exploitable. Step 2 (contain): Generate a strong random secret, export PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET and PLATFORM_ENV=production, restart the service (this invalidates all existing tokens, including any forged ones). If the host is internet-exposed, also gate behind authenticated reverse-proxy until patched. Step 3 (hunt): Pull reverse-proxy / WAF access logs for the host going back 30 days. Search for /auth/me, /workspaces/*/members, /workspaces/* (DELETE/PATCH) hits from external IPs. Cross-reference with /auth/register and /auth/login to identify sessions that authenticated without a preceding registration — likely forged-token usage.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "uvicorn"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("praisonai_platform.api.app", "praisonai_platform", "praisonai-platform")
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has "--reload")              // dev-mode flag, common on developer workstations
| extend SecretInCmdLine = ProcessCommandLine has "PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET"
| extend ProdEnvInCmdLine = ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)PLATFORM_ENV\s*=\s*(prod|production|stage|staging)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          SecretInCmdLine, ProdEnvInCmdLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where CommandLine has "uvicorn"
| where CommandLine has_any ("praisonai_platform.api.app", "praisonai_platform", "praisonai-platform")
| where not(CommandLine has "--reload")
| extend SecretInCmdLine = CommandLine has "PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET"
| extend ProdEnvInCmdLine = CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)PLATFORM_ENV\s*=\s*(prod|production|stage|staging)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, SubjectUserName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName,
          SecretInCmdLine, ProdEnvInCmdLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

praisonai-platform cross-tenant workspace operations from single source IP AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects JWT-forgery exploitation against CVE-2026-47410. After minting a token with arbitrary 'sub', the attacker hits authenticated routes — /auth/me to validate, then POST /workspaces/{id}/members, PATCH /workspaces/{id}, or DELETE /workspaces/{id} across multiple distinct workspace UUIDs. Catches the post-forgery pivot where one IP authenticates as many different user_ids in a short window — a pattern legitimate users do not produce. Rationale: Anchors on the exact route shapes the advisory's exploit chain calls out (steps 5-6: /auth/me + cross-workspace POST/PATCH/DELETE). The 'distinct workspaces >= 3 within 30m from one source IP' threshold captures the asymmetry between a legitimate user (their own 1-2 workspaces) and a forger pivoting across tenants. Falcon LogScale and CloudWatch left empty because FDR doesn't ship app-tier HTTP request logs and the CloudTrail/VPC schema doesn't carry the request path; this detection genuinely needs reverse-proxy/WAF telemetry the host SIEM aggregates.
ATT&CKT1078 T1190 T1212
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Load/performance testing tools (k6, Locust, JMeter) exercising the API end-to-end
  • Internal admin tooling that legitimately operates across many workspaces (back-office support console, billing reconciliation script)
  • Healthcheck monitors probing /auth/me with a sentinel token at high frequency
  • QA automation suites running end-to-end scenarios that create+delete workspaces in sequence
  • WAF/DAST scanners (Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP) crawling authenticated endpoints during a sanctioned pentest
Suppression filter
and not (UserAgent has_any ("k6", "Locust", "JMeter", "Burp", "ZAP", "HealthCheck", "kube-probe", "Prometheus")) and not (SourceIP in (dynamic(["<internal-monitoring-CIDR>", "<QA-runner-CIDR>"])))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full request timeline for the source IP for ±2h around FirstSeen. Confirm whether /auth/login or /auth/register from this IP preceded the authenticated activity — true forgery shows authenticated route hits with NO prior login. Cross-check the JWT 'sub' claim (if logged by the proxy) against the resolved user_ids on /auth/me responses; mismatches across many users from one IP confirm forgery. Step 2 (contain): Block the source IP and its /24 at the WAF immediately. Rotate PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET on the praisonai-platform deployment (this invalidates ALL outstanding tokens including the attacker's) and force re-authentication. Snapshot any workspaces touched by the destructive ops in case rollback is needed. Step 3 (hunt): Search the prior 30 days for the same IP/ASN against this deployment AND any other internal praisonai-platform instances. Pull the workspace audit trail for every WorkspaceId in the alert — flag any owner-membership changes, setting flips, or del
// Best-effort proxy via inbound network telemetry — true detection lives in web logs (see sentinel_kql).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("praisonai_platform", "praisonai-platform") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "uvicorn"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| summarize InboundCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), DistinctPorts = dcount(LocalPort)
   by DeviceName, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName
| where InboundCount > 50
| order by InboundCount desc
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
let WorkspaceRegex = @"/workspaces/([0-9a-f\-]{8,})";
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where RequestURL has_any ("/auth/me", "/auth/register", "/workspaces/")
| extend Method = toupper(coalesce(RequestMethod, DeviceCustomString1))
| extend WorkspaceId = extract(WorkspaceRegex, 1, RequestURL)
| extend IsDestructive = Method in ("DELETE", "PATCH") or (Method == "POST" and RequestURL has "/members")
| extend IsAuthMe = RequestURL has "/auth/me"
| extend IsRegister = RequestURL has "/auth/register"
| summarize
    AuthMeHits = countif(IsAuthMe),
    RegisterHits = countif(IsRegister),
    DistinctWorkspaces = dcountif(WorkspaceId, isnotempty(WorkspaceId)),
    DestructiveOps = countif(IsDestructive),
    SampleWorkspaces = make_set_if(WorkspaceId, isnotempty(WorkspaceId), 10),
    SampleURLs = make_set(RequestURL, 15),
    Methods = make_set(Method, 10),
    FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
    by SourceIP, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMinutes)
| where DistinctWorkspaces >= 3 and DestructiveOps >= 1   // 3 = empirical: a real user touches their own 1-2 workspaces; cross-tenant pivot starts at 3+
| order by LastSeen desc

PraisonAI Platform member role mutation endpoint hit (CVE-2026-47407 privilege escalation) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts HTTP PATCH/POST/DELETE calls against /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/members[/{user_id}] on PraisonAI Platform. Per CVE-2026-47407, these routes inherit the default `min_role="member"` so any basic member can promote themselves to admin/owner, demote/remove other members, or delete the workspace. Any hit on these endpoints by a non-owner principal is high-fidelity for exploitation. Rationale: Article explicitly names routes/workspaces.py:115-141 update_member_role / add_member / remove_member / delete_workspace as the buggy member-management endpoints; any non-admin caller hitting them is exploit-shaped. Pattern is the FastAPI prefix /api/v1/workspaces/{uuid}/members[/{uuid}] taken directly from the affected-functionality table in the GHSA.
ATT&CKT1078 T1098 T1548
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate workspace owner adding a teammate via POST /members
  • Workspace owner changing a member's display role on PATCH /members/{user_id}
  • Owner offboarding a user via DELETE /members/{user_id}
  • Automated provisioning script driven by an SSO/SCIM connector using an owner-tier API token
  • Admin UI bulk-updating members during a team reorg
Suppression filter
// Sentinel ImWebSession refinement once owner identity is enriched from the platform DB:
// | join kind=leftanti (WorkspaceOwners_CL | project SrcUsername=OwnerUserId_s, url_workspace_id=WorkspaceId_s) on SrcUsername, url_workspace_id
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE — pull the request and the requesting principal: extract the bearer token's user ID (SrcUsername / X-Auth-User header), then query the platform DB or admin API for that user's role in url_workspace_id. If the user is `member`, treat as confirmed CVE-2026-47407 exploitation. Note user_agent and source IP. 2) CONTAIN — revoke the offending bearer token, disable the user, and roll back the member-role mutation (restore previous role, re-add removed members). If the workspace was deleted, restore from backup. Apply the GHSA patch / set min_role="admin" on the affected routes. 3) HUNT — pivot on the same source IP and account for prior /auth/register, /workspaces/{id}/agents/{id} GET/PATCH, and /projects/{id}/stats reads in the last 7d to identify cross-tenant data accessed before escalation.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where HttpMethod in ("PATCH","POST","DELETE")
| where Url matches regex @"/api/v1/workspaces/[0-9a-f-]{36}/members(?:/[0-9a-f-]{36})?/?$"
| where HttpStatusCode between (200 .. 299)
| extend url_workspace_id = extract(@"/api/v1/workspaces/([0-9a-f-]{36})/members", 1, Url),
         target_user_id  = extract(@"/members/([0-9a-f-]{36})", 1, Url)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, HttpMethod, Url,
          url_workspace_id, target_user_id, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, DstHostname
| order by TimeGenerated desc

PraisonAI Platform cross-workspace nested-resource enumeration (CVE-2026-47407 IDOR) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts a single authenticated user repeatedly hitting nested-resource routes (/agents/{id}, /issues/{id}, /projects/{id}, /labels/{id}, /dependencies/...) under one workspace prefix while supplying many distinct inner UUIDs. CVE-2026-47407's IDOR pattern requires the attacker to keep their own workspace_id in the URL and rotate the inner resource UUID; this enumeration shape is the exploit fingerprint and cannot be produced by normal single-workspace usage at any meaningful rate. Rationale: Article's PoC step 6 explicitly shows GET /api/v1/workspaces/{Mallory_ws}/agents/{Alice_agent_id} succeeding cross-tenant — the exploit fingerprint is many distinct inner_id under a single (or pair of) workspace_id prefix(es). Article enumerates the exact resource_kind set (agents/issues/projects/labels/dependencies in the affected-routes table). Threshold (15 distinct in 10m, ≤2 url workspaces) targets the enumeration shape rather than per-request lookup.
ATT&CKT1190 T1213 T1530
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Power user mass-triaging a backlog (Jira-like sweep through many issues in their own workspace)
  • Automated reporting/export job iterating every project in one workspace
  • CI pipeline running platform integration tests that touch many resources
  • Workspace migration scripts re-reading every agent before a re-encrypt
  • Browser dev-tools or load-test traffic from QA
Suppression filter
// Sentinel — exclude known service principals / CI runner accounts once enriched:
// | where SrcUsername !in ("svc-ci-runner","svc-export-bot")
// | where SrcIpAddr !in (CI_Egress_IPs_CL | project IP)
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE — pull the SrcUsername and identify their actual workspace memberships from the platform DB; for each inner_id touched, fetch the resource row and compare its `workspace_id` against the URL's url_workspace_id. Any mismatch = confirmed CVE-2026-47407 IDOR exploitation. List the cross-tenant resources read or modified (PATCH/DELETE responses 2xx). 2) CONTAIN — revoke the user's bearer tokens, freeze the user, and snapshot affected resources before recovery. If `agent.instructions` was rewritten (PoC step 7's exfil pivot), quarantine downstream LLM calls that used those agents and rotate any API keys referenced in the original instructions. Apply the GHSA patch enforcing `resource.workspace_id == url_workspace_id` in every nested service lookup. 3) HUNT — pivot on the same src IP and account-creation IP for /auth/register events in the last 30d, then enumerate every member-management call and cross-workspace agent/issue/project access from those identities.
let LookbackHours = 24h;
let WindowMinutes = 10m;
let MinDistinctInnerIds = 15;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
| where HttpMethod in ("GET","PATCH","DELETE")
| where Url matches regex @"/api/v1/workspaces/[0-9a-f-]{36}/(agents|issues|projects|labels|dependencies)/[0-9a-f-]{36}"
| extend url_workspace_id = extract(@"/api/v1/workspaces/([0-9a-f-]{36})", 1, Url),
         resource_kind   = extract(@"/(agents|issues|projects|labels|dependencies)/[0-9a-f-]{36}", 1, Url),
         inner_id        = extract(@"/(?:agents|issues|projects|labels|dependencies)/([0-9a-f-]{36})", 1, Url)
| summarize distinct_inner_ids   = dcount(inner_id),
            distinct_workspaces  = dcount(url_workspace_id),
            hits                 = count(),
            kinds                = make_set(resource_kind, 10),
            first_seen           = min(TimeGenerated),
            last_seen            = max(TimeGenerated)
          by SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMinutes)
// 15 = empirical: a normal user rarely opens >15 distinct agents/issues in 10m; IDOR-style enumeration easily exceeds it
| where distinct_inner_ids >= MinDistinctInnerIds and distinct_workspaces <= 2
| order by distinct_inner_ids desc
@http.method:(GET OR PATCH OR DELETE) @http.url_details.path:(*/api/v1/workspaces/*/agents/* OR */api/v1/workspaces/*/issues/* OR */api/v1/workspaces/*/projects/* OR */api/v1/workspaces/*/labels/* OR */api/v1/workspaces/*/dependencies/*) @http.status_code:[200 TO 299]
# log group: /aws/elasticloadbalancing/<alb-name>
fields @timestamp, client_ip, request_verb, request_url, target_status_code
| filter request_url like /\/api\/v1\/workspaces\/[0-9a-f-]+\/(agents|issues|projects|labels|dependencies)\/[0-9a-f-]+/
      and request_verb in ["GET", "PATCH", "DELETE"]
      and target_status_code >= 200
      and target_status_code < 300
| parse request_url /\/workspaces\/(?<url_ws>[0-9a-f-]+)\/(?<kind>agents|issues|projects|labels|dependencies)\/(?<inner_id>[0-9a-f-]+)/
| stats count(*) as hits, count_distinct(inner_id) as distinct_inner_ids, count_distinct(url_ws) as distinct_workspaces by client_ip, bin(10m)
| filter distinct_inner_ids >= 15 and distinct_workspaces <= 2
| sort distinct_inner_ids desc

PraisonAI Platform open-registration burst followed by workspace privileged action AIDelivery High
Hunts the bootstrap pattern in CVE-2026-47407 / GHSA-h8q5-cp56-rr65: anonymous POST /api/v1/auth/register succeeds (open registration with no email verification) and within minutes the same source IP / new account starts touching member-management or cross-workspace nested-resource routes. Catches automated exploitation kits and attacker-from-the-internet abuse of the 0.0.0.0:8000 default bind. Rationale: Article calls out `/api/v1/auth/register` as open + no email verification (routes/auth.py:19-29) and the default 0.0.0.0:8000 bind (__main__.py:13-16) — the GHSA explicitly states "one curl from any unauthenticated network position is enough to bootstrap into the system." Pairing a register success with sensitive nested-route activity from the same source IP within 10 minutes is the exact bootstrap-to-abuse pivot.
ATT&CKT1190 T1136 T1078
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A real new user signing up and immediately creating their first workspace + agent (POST /workspaces/.../agents is legitimate setup)
  • QA / load-test traffic from an internal staging IP exercising the signup flow
  • Marketing-driven signup campaign producing a burst of new accounts
  • Pen test exercising the same registration path with explicit authorization
  • Smoke-test CI hitting register + immediate cleanup
Suppression filter
// Sentinel — exclude internal QA egress and known signup-test source ranges:
// | where SrcIpAddr !in (QA_Egress_IPs_CL | project IP)
// | where RegisterUserAgent !startswith "k6/" and RegisterUserAgent !startswith "Locust/"
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE — fetch the new account's email, user_id, and source IP from the /auth/register response; geolocate the IP and check against known corporate / customer ranges. Pull every subsequent request from that IP within the next hour and tag any /workspaces/{id}/members*, /agents/{id} PATCH, or DELETE call as exploitation evidence. 2) CONTAIN — disable the newly-created account, invalidate any bearer token it minted, and block the source IP at the perimeter. If the account already PATCH'd a member role or modified another tenant's agent.instructions, roll back the change and notify the affected workspace owner; per PoC step 7, hijacked agent.instructions can include a `POST exfil` URL — quarantine any LLM responses generated against affected agents. 3) HUNT — search the past 30d for additional /auth/register successes from the same IP/ASN, the same user-agent string, and any cluster of accounts that touched the same victim workspace_ids. Confirm the GHSA patch is applied and that `/aut

Unauthenticated JSON-RPC POST to PraisonAI /a2a endpoint (CVE-2026-47391 exploit) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts inbound HTTP POSTs to the PraisonAI A2A example endpoint `/a2a` carrying a JSON-RPC `message/send` payload from sources outside the local subnet — the exact remote entry point used in CVE-2026-47391. The official example binds 0.0.0.0:8000 with no `auth_token`, so any external POST to this path is suspect. Rationale: Pivots on the exact endpoint path `/a2a` named in the GHSA advisory (line 194 of a2a.py) plus POST method (the JSON-RPC `message/send` verb the exploit requires). External source-IP filter eliminates internal smoke tests; status=200 filter ensures the server actually processed the request. Cross-checked GHSA-vg22-4gmj-prxw and the inline source listing in the article body. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vg22-4gmj-prxw
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.006
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate authenticated A2A client integrations from a customer-facing reverse proxy where the source IP is genuinely public
  • Security scanners (Qualys, Tenable, Burp) probing the /a2a path during scheduled internal pentests
  • DevOps health checks routed through a public load balancer that strips XFF and presents the LB's public IP
  • Researchers/red team validating the patch after upgrading PraisonAI
Suppression filter
| where not(HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent has_any ("Qualys","Nessus","Burp","ZAP","Nuclei","masscan")) and SrcIpAddr !in (dynamic(["<known_scanner_ip_1>","<known_scanner_ip_2>"]))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full HTTP request body for the matching POST and confirm it contains `"method":"message/send"` and a `params.message` field; check the source IP against threat-intel and known scanner ranges. Step 2 (contain): Immediately add a WAF block rule for POST to `/a2a` from non-allowlisted sources; identify the PraisonAI process and verify whether `auth_token` is configured — if not, stop the service and rebind to 127.0.0.1 until upgraded past the patched release. Step 3 (hunt): For any host that received a 200 on `/a2a` from a public source, pivot to DeviceProcessEvents for child processes of the uvicorn/python parent in the same time window (any non-Python child = likely eval() RCE); check for new files under the working directory matching `*canary*`, `*.txt` markers, or unexpected `id`/`whoami` output captured in stdout logs.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("InboundConnectionAccepted","ConnectionSuccess")
| where LocalPort in (8000, 80, 443, 8080)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","python3","python","uvicorn.exe","uvicorn")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("a2a-server.py","a2a.py","praisonai","praisonaiagents")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalIP, LocalPort,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
let A2APaths = dynamic(["/a2a", "/a2a/", "/a2a?"]);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
| where Url has "/a2a" or UrlOriginal has "/a2a"
| where DstPortNumber in (8000, 80, 443, 8080)
| where not(ipv4_is_private(SrcIpAddr))
| where HttpStatusCode between (200 .. 299)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber,
          Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpRequestBodyBytes,
          EventVendor, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Suspicious child process spawned by PraisonAI uvicorn/python A2A server (eval() RCE evidence) AIExploitation High
Hunts for shell, network, or recon utilities spawned as children of the PraisonAI A2A server process — the post-exploitation footprint of the `calculate(expression)` tool's `eval(expression)` executing attacker-controlled Python. Legitimate uvicorn-hosted FastAPI apps almost never spawn `sh`, `bash`, `cmd.exe`, `curl`, `wget`, `nc`, `whoami`, `id`, etc. Rationale: Parent-child shape comes directly from the article's vulnerable code (lines 23-26 `eval(expression)`, lines 30-34 agent registration, line 51-53 uvicorn bind, line 314 `agent.chat`). The article literally states `calculate in DEFAULT_DANGEROUS_TOOLS: False` confirming there is no built-in guard — so any non-Python child of the uvicorn-hosted a2a-server.py is post-exploitation. Sensitive-string list pulled from the article's own "potential credential or environment variable exposure" impact statement. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vg22-4gmj-prxw
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer SSHed into the box running shell commands inside the same uvicorn-hosted Python REPL for debugging
  • Legitimate registered tools that intentionally shell out (e.g. a `search_web` implementation that invokes curl)
  • Container init scripts running `whoami`/`id`/`hostname` for startup logging when the A2A process is the container PID 1
  • Sysadmin running `env`/`printenv` from within the A2A virtualenv to verify GEMINI_API_KEY is set
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--reload","--debug")) and not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("healthcheck","liveness","readiness"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Capture the full child ProcessCommandLine and InitiatingProcessCommandLine; if the child is a shell with no interactive TTY and the parent is uvicorn serving on 0.0.0.0, treat as confirmed RCE. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host from network via EDR (Defender `Isolate machine` action); preserve the running uvicorn process memory before kill for forensics; rotate any API keys (GEMINI_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) present in the process environment. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot to DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound connections from the same `InitiatingProcessId` (data exfil), check DeviceFileEvents for new files written to the working directory (especially `*canary*` or `*.txt` markers matching the PoC), and search inbound `/a2a` POSTs in the 5-minute window before the suspicious child spawn to identify the attacker source IP.

PraisonAI A2A example server started with vulnerable 0.0.0.0 bind and no auth_token AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the launch of the vulnerable PraisonAI A2A example process itself — Python invoking `a2a-server.py` (or the `A2A().serve()` API) on a public-facing host. The article's `__main__` block (`uvicorn.run(app, host='0.0.0.0', port=8000)`) is the deployment fingerprint; flagging it lets the SOC catch unpatched / mis-deployed instances before they're exploited. Rationale: Maps directly to the vulnerable example's __main__ block (`uvicorn.run(app, host='0.0.0.0', port=8000)`) and the A2A class's `serve(host='0.0.0.0', port=8000)` default named in the article body (a2a.py line 125). Cross-checked GHSA-vg22-4gmj-prxw which confirms the example's exact path `examples/python/a2a/a2a-server.py`. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vg22-4gmj-prxw
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal dev/lab boxes where engineers intentionally test PraisonAI examples (legit but should be flagged as policy violation)
  • Container images that bake the example server as a documented demo target
  • Properly configured production deployments where auth_token IS set but the 0.0.0.0 bind is intentional behind an authenticated reverse proxy
  • CI/CD pipelines that boot the example briefly to run smoke tests
Suppression filter
| where not(DeviceName has_any ("dev-","lab-","test-","ci-")) and not(ProcessCommandLine has "127.0.0.1")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify the host and ask the owner whether this is a known PraisonAI deployment; check if the listening socket on port 8000 is actually reachable externally via a port scan from outside the perimeter. Step 2 (contain): If the host is internet-reachable on port 8000 and `auth_token` is not configured, treat as an open RCE — coordinate with the application owner to either set `auth_token`, rebind to `127.0.0.1`, or remove the `calculate` eval()-based tool from the agent. Upgrade past v4.6.37 if a patched release is available. Step 3 (hunt): Pull 30-day inbound web logs for the host's port 8000 looking for any external POST to `/a2a` (link to UC #1); pull 30 days of process events for the same uvicorn pid for unusual child processes (link to UC #2); audit `tasks/list`/`tasks/get`/`tasks/cancel` endpoint access mentioned in the advisory for prior reconnaissance attempts.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","python","python3","uvicorn.exe","uvicorn")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("a2a-server.py","praisonaiagents","praisonai") 
     or (ProcessCommandLine has "A2A" and ProcessCommandLine has "serve")
| extend BindsAllInterfaces = ProcessCommandLine has_any ("0.0.0.0","--host 0.0.0.0")
| extend ConfiguresAuth = ProcessCommandLine has_any ("auth_token","AUTH_TOKEN")
| where BindsAllInterfaces == true or ConfiguresAuth == false
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Hits = count(),
            AnyCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine), AnyParent = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
            by DeviceName, AccountName, FileName
| order by LastSeen desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("python","python3","uvicorn")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("a2a-server.py","praisonaiagents","praisonai")
     or (TargetProcessCommandLine has "A2A" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "serve")
| extend BindsAllInterfaces = TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("0.0.0.0","--host 0.0.0.0")
| where BindsAllInterfaces == true
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Hits = count(),
            AnyCmd = any(TargetProcessCommandLine), AnyParent = any(ParentProcessCommandLine)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName
| order by LastSeen desc

Use this to drive proactive patching before exploitation is observed. Rationale: Uses the exact affected package names (`praisonaiagents`, `PraisonAI`) and version ceiling (1.6.39) called out in the advisory. Cross-checked against the GitLab advisory entry for CVE-2026-39888 confirming `praisonaiagents` PyPI package name and the chain of related CVEs in `execute_code`. PraisonAI Python subprocess spawns OS shell with discovery / credential-reading commands AIExploitation High
Hunts the post-exploitation footprint of CVE-2026-47392: once the AST sandbox is escaped via `print.__self__`, the attacker calls `os.popen(...)` which forks a system shell as a child of the praisonaiagents Python subprocess. Detects python.exe/python3 spawning sh/cmd with classic recon, env-dump, or cloud-credential read commands. Rationale: Anchored on the exact PoC behaviour in the advisory: `mod.popen("id")` from inside the escaped Python sandbox spawns a shell child of the praisonaiagents Python subprocess. The dual-filter (suspicious child cmd + praisonaiagents parent context) makes this high-fidelity even though python→shell alone is noisy. Cross-checked against the CVE-2026-39888/34938 advisories which confirm the same `execute_code` subprocess sandbox model. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/pkg/pypi/praisonaiagents/CVE-2026-39888/ • https://www.thehackerwire.com/praisonai-critical-rce-via-sandbox-bypass-cve-2026-34938/
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1059.004 T1068 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A PraisonAI tool that legitimately wraps a shell command (some custom tools call `subprocess.run('ls')` by design — review the tool registry)
  • An agent test harness that intentionally runs `whoami` to verify sandbox is working
  • Container image build steps that spawn a Python entrypoint which itself shells out (the parent-cmdline filter on `praisonai` should suppress most of these)
  • DevOps Ansible/SaltStack runs invoking Python wrappers that probe `/etc/passwd` for user enumeration
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--version", "--help") and not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("AWS_SECRET","/run/secrets","/dev/tcp/")))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the full process tree (parent python + spawned shell + any grandchild) and the praisonaiagents service account. Capture the shell's stdout if available (auditd / `osquery process_events`). Pull the most recent inbound request to the agent endpoint that correlates by time. Step 2 — Contain: kill the python parent PID, isolate the host via EDR network containment, rotate any credentials in env vars the shell read (OPENAI_API_KEY, AWS_*, AZURE_*, K8s service-account tokens at `/run/secrets/`). Step 3 — Hunt: check DeviceFileEvents for new .py temp drops with `print.__self__` (UC3), DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound from the same python PID to unfamiliar IPs, and AAD/IAM logs for the rotated keys being used elsewhere in the prior 7 days.

Literal PraisonAI sandbox-escape signature: `print.__self__` + builtins dict access AIExploitation Medium
Hunts for the literal exploit primitive from CVE-2026-47392 — `print.__self__` followed by `vars(` on the returned builtins module — in Python process command lines and recently-written .py files. Catches both naive PoC reuse and lightly-mutated variants since the `print.__self__` token is highly distinctive in benign Python code. Rationale: Targets the four article-specific tokens from the PoC walkthrough: `print.__self__`, `.__self__.vars`, `vars(print`, and the construction pattern. These tokens appear in essentially zero benign Python code — `__self__` on a built-in function is an obscure CPython internal that real developers don't write against. Cross-checked the CVE-2026-39888 article series confirming the same `execute_code` sandbox is the attack surface and all bypasses share this Python-cmdline-or-tempfile telemetry shape. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/pkg/pypi/praisonaiagents/CVE-2026-39888/ • https://www.thehackerwire.com/praisonai-ast-sandbox-bypass-leads-to-rce/
ATT&CKT1068 T1027 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher reproducing the PoC on a lab host (the literal advisory PoC string)
  • Python language internals tutorial / blog content executed in a notebook
  • Penetration test reproducing CVE-2026-47392 against the production AI agent
  • An internal red-team exercise running the GHSA PoC verbatim against a staging deployment
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has "jupyter" and FolderPath !has "jupyter" and ProcessCommandLine !contains "# CVE-2026-47392 reproduction"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: capture the full ProcessCommandLine (or temp .py file contents via DeviceFileEvents → file collection action) and confirm the token isn't a docstring/comment by reading 5-10 lines of context. Identify which AI agent / endpoint received the input that produced this code. Step 2 — Contain: if confirmed exploit, take the same actions as UC2 — kill PID, network-isolate, rotate exposed secrets — and immediately quarantine the input source (block the requesting IP/user at the agent gateway). Step 3 — Hunt: search input/prompt logs for the originating request body; pivot on the requester's user identity / IP to find prior probing attempts (e.g. earlier CVE-2026-39888 / 34938 / 40158 patterns: `__traceback__`, `tb_frame`, `f_back`, `f_builtins`, `type.__getattribute__`).
union
(
  DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where FileName in~ ("python","python3","python.exe","python3.exe","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("print.__self__", ".__self__.vars", "vars(print", "__self__\nd")
     or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"print\s*\.\s*__self__"
  | extend Source = "cmdline"
  | project Timestamp, Source, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
),
(
  DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
  | where FileName endswith ".py"
     or FolderPath has_any ("/tmp/", @"\Temp\", "/var/folders/")
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python.exe","python3.exe")
  | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("praisonai","_execute_code_sandboxed","python_tools","execute_code")
  | extend Source = "file-write"
  | project Timestamp, Source, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessCommandLine=""
)
| order by Timestamp desc
union
(
  ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where TargetProcessName has_any ("python","python3","python.exe")
  | where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("print.__self__", ".__self__.vars", "vars(print")
     or TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex @"print\s*\.\s*__self__"
  | extend Source = "cmdline"
  | project TimeGenerated, Source, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessCommandLine
),
(
  ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
  | where TargetFileName endswith ".py"
     or TargetFilePath has_any ("/tmp/", @"\Temp\", "/var/folders/")
  | where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3","python.exe")
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("praisonai","_execute_code_sandboxed","python_tools","execute_code")
  | extend Source = "file-write"
  | project TimeGenerated, Source, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessCommandLine=""
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: PraisonAI Sandbox Escape Signature - print.__self__ builtins leak (CVE-2026-47392)
id: 8a5f3c2e-4d91-4b7f-9e0a-2c8f6d4e1b73
description: Detects the literal exploit primitive for CVE-2026-47392 — use of print.__self__ to retrieve the real Python builtins module from inside the PraisonAI execute_code sandbox, typically followed by vars() to expose __import__.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4mr5-g6f9-cfrh
  - https://advisories.gitlab.com/pkg/pypi/praisonaiagents/CVE-2026-39888/

PraisonAI `deploy --type api` command execution — vulnerable server provisioned AIInstallation High
Hunts for the documented PraisonAI quickstart command (`praisonai deploy --type api`) which generates a Flask server that defaults to AUTH_ENABLED=False. Surfaces vulnerable deployments inside the estate before scanners find them externally. Rationale: Anchors on the exact vendor-documented quickstart `praisonai deploy --type api` (and `-t api` short flag) cited in GHSA-8444-4fhq-fxpq §Summary. Cross-checked against Sysdig (rapid-exploitation timeline) and parent GHSA-6rmh-7xcm-cpxj. Pure CLI pattern — no hashes to bypass. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6rmh-7xcm-cpxj • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/cve-2026-44338-praisonai-authentication-bypass-in-under-4-hours-and-the-growing-trend-of-rapid-exploitation • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/praisonai-cve-2026-44338-auth-bypass.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate dev/test deployment of PraisonAI ≥4.6.34 (patched version) where operator opted into auth_enabled=True
  • CI/CD pipeline executing the quickstart for integration testing
  • Security researcher / red team running PoC in sanctioned lab
  • Documentation walkthrough by developers learning the framework
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("code.exe", "devenv.exe") and not (DeviceName has_any ("dev-", "lab-", "sandbox-"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): On the host, run `pip show praisonai` to extract the installed version. Versions 2.5.6–4.6.33 are vulnerable; 4.6.34+ patched. Inspect the generated server file for `AUTH_ENABLED = False` and `AUTH_TOKEN = None` literals. Step 2 (contain): If vulnerable and reachable, stop the Flask process (`pkill -f 'praisonai.*deploy'`), revoke any LLM API keys exposed in the host's env (OPENAI_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY rotated immediately), and block port 8005 inbound at host firewall. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot to UC2/UC3 to confirm no exploitation occurred — search inbound :8005 connections from public IPs and HTTP POSTs to /chat or /agents in the last 30 days.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "praisonai"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "deploy"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--type api", "-t api")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountUpn, FolderPath, FileName,
          ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where CommandLine has "praisonai"
| where CommandLine has "deploy"
| where CommandLine has_any ("--type api", "-t api")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
